22_marg367: BEDE. The book of Tobias is wholesome on the surface of the letter, for it abounds in the greatest examples and admonitions of the moral life. But as much as fruit excels leaves, so much does the allegory excel the history; for it contains the greatest sacraments of the Church. For Tobias himself signifies the people of Israel, which, while the other nations were given to idolatry, served God with right faith and works. Hence: when all went to the golden calves, etc. For Jeroboam, who made golden calves for the deceiving of his subjects, expresses the worshippers of idolatry, whose accomplices are signified in his subjects.

22_marg383: BEDE. Let no one wonder if sometimes a good thing typically signifies evil, and evil things good. For if this were not allowed, the name of God would never be written with black ink but always with shining gold, because God is light. But if you write the name of the devil with a white stone, it nonetheless signifies darkness. Tobias blinded, therefore, signifies the people of Israel: 'For blindness in part has happened in Israel.' Wearied from burying, he was blinded. For he who persists unwearied in good works does not lose the light of faith. So spiritually he sleeps wearied who neglects to watch, to stand, to act manfully and to be strengthened, to whom it is said: 'Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead', etc.

22_marg394: BEDE. The angel appeared to Tobias and offered himself as his companion; and the Son of God assumed man and, conversing visibly with men, saved the human race. Tobias brought the angel in to his father, etc.; and the Lord, through the miracles which he did in the flesh, showed the people of the Jews, from whom he had taken flesh, that he is the son and the angel, that is, the messenger, of the Father's will; to whom also he preached the joy of everlasting salvation, saying: 'Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' And to those despairing of the heavenly light: 'I am,' he says, 'the light of the world. He that followeth me walketh not in darkness.'

22_marg395: BEDE. The angel promises Tobias to lead his son into the city of the Medes and to bring him back. Christ promises the believing Jews, although most are blinded, that he will open the sacraments of his incarnation to the gentiles, and at the end of times will disclose them more widely to the people of the Jews, the faith of his divinity accompanying and cooperating. Led to the Medes, he says: 'Other sheep I have that are not of this fold.' Of the bringing back the Apostle says: 'Until the fulness of the gentiles should come in, and so all Israel should be saved.' When Tobias asked the angel whence he was, 'I am,' he said, 'Azarias, the son of the great Ananias.' Azarias is 'helper', Ananias 'glory of God'; Christ also shows his faithful that he himself is the one of whom it is said: 'Thou art my helper and my deliverer: O Lord, make no delay.' And: 'We saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father.'
22_marg396: BEDE. When the Lord appeared in the flesh, all things were made ready that were necessary for our redemption, and by which the faith and life of the Church may be nourished and strengthened until the way of this world is ended: that is, his miracles, doctrine, temptation, passion, resurrection, ascension, the sending of the Holy Spirit, the faith of believers, the persecution of unbelievers. These being accomplished in Judea, the mediator of God and men preached through the apostles to the Jews his kinsmen and to the gentiles the joys of heavenly salvation and peace, and gave them by himself to those who were willing to receive and believe; and so he came through the apostles to the salvation of the gentiles.

22_marg398: BEDE. The sacrament of the Lord's passion is plainly signified. For the fish which, desiring to devour Tobias, was killed at the angel's teaching, signifies the devil, who, while he sought the flesh in our Redeemer, was caught by the power of the divinity. The Tigris is a river which from its most rapid course is so named from the tiger, a most swift beast; it signifies the downward course of our mortality, in which the monstrous fish lay hid when the devil, the invisible seducer of the human race, held the empire of death. Tobias lodged by the streams of the Tigris because the Lord, appearing to the world, led his life among mortals; but the wave of sin did not flood him, nor did the prince of the world, coming, have anything in him.
22_marg399: BEDE. Christ accepted death, to which he owed nothing, that he might wash his feet, namely his members, from the contagion of sin and death. The fish ran at him desiring to devour him; and when the Lord suffered on the cross, the devil, at whose prompting he had been crucified, came, seeking whether he might find any sin in him.
22_marg400: Christ, when the moment of death was at hand, began to fear and to be heavy, not at the devil but at death, which by the envy of the devil entered into the world, shuddering at it from the natural frailty of the flesh; hence: Father, remove this chalice from me.
22_marg401: Christ seized the devil, who wished to take him on the cross, and by dying conquered him. He seized therefore the gill, that with the right hand of his power he might separate the most wicked head from the body; that is, that he might take away the wickedness of the ancient enemy from those whom he had made his body, and bring these into his own body, that is, the Church. For the fish has its gill at the border of the head and the body. And Christ is the head of the Church, which is his body, and the devil the head of the wicked, who are his body.

22_marg403: BEDE. The Lord took out the entrails of the fish when he disclosed more widely to the saints the wickedness of the devil and, as it were, laid open the secrets of his snares. He laid up his heart for himself because he made known his craftiness in the Scriptures, of which it is said: 'The serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth.' And elsewhere: 'Are we ignorant of his devices?' He laid up the gall also, because he willed it to be written and kept, for the study of caution, with how great fury of malice he rages against the human race. He laid up the liver, because through the doctors of truth he made known his malignant counsels against us. For the physicians say that by the heat and hidden power of the liver foods are cooked and digested. And when with careful thought we search out in what order the things we plan to do are to be done, we as it were cook with the heat of the liver the foods received in the stomach.

22_marg408: BEDE. The people of the gentiles, hearing the word of faith and admonished by the apostles to give Christ a wife from its stock, could not take up the laws of the new faith without sure examination, because it had once had many doctors who, all comprehended as it were in the number seven, knew this life only and said nothing certain of the eternal; and therefore, without hope of immortal life, the destruction of eternal death carried them off. But with the truth teaching within and sounding without through the mouths of the doctors, at length it understood that it is just that those who spoke foolish things should perish foolishly.

22_marg410: BEDE. Tobias, being brought into the chamber, took out of, etc. God, about to receive the Church from the gentiles, at the beginning of the espousal commands her to renounce the devil and all his pomps, and to confess the faith of the holy Trinity unto the remission of sins; which is to burn the inmost entrails of the fish on live coals.

22_marg411: BEDE. Because after the renunciation of the devil, after the confession of the true faith, there follows the remission of sins through the water of baptism, the devil having been driven out. He bound the devil because he restrained him so that he ceased from harming the faithful; whom, although he is sometimes permitted to tempt them for their proving, he is nevertheless forbidden to overcome.
22_marg412: The desert and Egypt signify the hearts of unbelievers, which are deserted by God because they are unworthy of his dwelling, and, according to the interpretation of Egypt, darkened with the darkness of their unbelief. And fittingly he who is deserted by God is filled by a demon. And the angel bound in the desert the demon who wished to kill Tobias: he who, having restrained the devil from the faithful, who are the members of Christ, permits him to rule only in unbelievers; in whom nevertheless he holds him bound, because he is not permitted to harm even them as much as he strives.
22_interl614: either mystically or according to the letter.
22_marg413: The crowing of the cocks is the sound of the preachers, who after the darkness of errors announce the day of light to come. There were among the gentiles those who doubted whether the Lord had truly conquered the ancient enemy, and therefore thought it better to bury and hide the faith of his name; but afterwards, having recognized the light of truth, as with the dawn going before and the crowing of the cocks growing frequent, that is, by the voice of the preachers, they knew truly that Christ, the enemy being overcome, is the bridegroom of holy Church.
22_marg414: BEDE. Raguel rejoices at the life of Tobias and the union of his daughter, and blessing God he kills two kine and four rams. He prepares a feast for all his friends and neighbors. The people of the gentiles rejoices at the faith of Christ and at the devotion of its nation advancing in the faith of the Lord, so that from among them also doctors should arise who afterwards would become martyrs. These are kine, because they bore the yoke of the gospel and by preaching begot others who would bear it. They are rams, as being leaders and fathers of the peoples; hence: 'Bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.' They are fat, filled with the grace of heavenly love; hence: 'Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness.'
22_marg415: TWO KINE also. BEDE. The Apostle of the gentiles taught those who had come to the faith from its stock to be such that the envious enemy would tempt them for the excellence of their virtue, and having tempted them would not conquer them, but would make them victors and martyrs. He also caused to be killed those whom he taught to crucify their flesh for Christ with its vices and concupiscences. By their killing he prepared a feast, because the life, progress, passion and crown of the saints give gladness to many, who receive a feast from those by whose examples they are refreshed.
22_marg416: Because the holy doctors and martyrs keep the four books of the gospel in faith and work; they are fortified with prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance; and they instruct the Church of God in the four parts of the world.
22_marg417: Because some of their own accord mortify their bodies that they may be a living sacrifice; others undergo martyrdom at the hands of unbelievers, conquering the ancient enemy by the armour of justice on the right hand and on the left, that is, in prosperity and in adversity.
22_marg418: BEDE. We adjure Christ to remain with us until through the grace of the Holy Spirit we obtain the perfection of rest, in which we may rest both from sins in the body and from wicked thoughts in the mind.

22_marg426: BEDE. Having heard the word of salvation from the doctors, the people of the Jews rises from the long blindness of its unbelief and runs with love to the Lord, but stumbling in the steps of its works, until, reborn and instructed in Christ, it receives the light of faith and of working.
22_marg427: BEDE. The Lord openly reveals to believers how great is the malice of the ancient enemy, who longed to devour him in his passion, but being slain thereby lost his members, that is, those whom he formerly held.
22_interl648: The people of the Jews, after it has known the most bitter malice of the ancient enemy, recovered the light it had lost.
22_interl649: BEDE. In which hope is signified, because it does not yet live and is without soul, but is hoped for. 'But if we hope for that which we see not, we wait for it with patience.' The gospel parable also, under the name of bread and of wine [so the edition] and of an egg, expresses the three highest virtues, namely charity, faith and hope.
22_marg428: BEDE. The people of the Jews still has a veil before the face of its heart, so that it does not understand the grace of Christ. It has a white skin, because it seems to itself white and just; like the skin of an egg, because it bears blindness of mind under the most foolish hope of a Christ still to be born, who will free the Jews and give them a great empire. But when the veil shall be taken away, they will acknowledge that Christ has already come and redeemed the world with his blood. Hence there follows that, having received sight, Tobias with his wife glorified God.
22_marg429: WHITE SKIN etc. BEDE. The white skin designates the folly of a people pleasing itself, having a zeal of God but not according to knowledge, of whom it is said: 'Seeking to establish their own justice, they have not submitted themselves to the justice of God.' For the black pupil sees, the white is dark; and those who seem wise to themselves and say, 'Are we also blind?', in them the truth is not. But those who, conscious of frailty and ignorance, say, 'O Lord my God, enlighten my darkness', are enlightened by the Lord.
